item_7.notes:
[chunk 1/1] FILING: NVDA 10-K FY2024 (filed 2024-02-21). Key findings from Item 7 MD&A:

1. CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION (severity 4): A single unnamed indirect customer estimated at ~19% of total FY2024 revenue ($11.6B implied), purchasing through Customer A (13% direct) and other system integrators/distributors. Both concentrated in Compute & Networking. NVIDIA explicitly states "Our estimated Compute & Networking demand is expected to remain concentrated."

2. CLOUD PROVIDER CONCENTRATION (severity 3): Large cloud providers >50% of Data Center revenue in Q4 FY2024. Data Center = $47.5B (~78% of total), implying cloud hyperscalers represent ~39%+ of total company revenue. No individual names disclosed in this section; Note 9 / Note 8 referenced for investment details not included in this extract.

3. CAPEX ROI GAP (severity 3): $2.2B inventory/purchase obligation provisions in FY2024. Non-cancellable orders placed beyond 12-month historical lead times with prepayments and premiums. Next-gen products described as "supply-constrained" based on demand indications — committed supply without confirmed contracted revenue.

4. COST OPACITY (severity 2): February 2023 depreciation life extension (server equipment 3yr→4-5yr; assembly equipment 5yr→7yr) inflated FY2024 operating income by $135M and net income by $114M. This is a one-time accounting change with multi-year P&L tailwind that flatters reported margins.

5. CHINA EXPORT CONTROLS (severity 4): China fell from 19% to 14% of Data Center revenue YoY, then to "mid-single digit" in Q4 FY2024. Risk of total exclusion from China market if controls tighten further.

6. SUPPLIER CONCENTRATION (severity 3): Supply chain "currently concentrated in the Asia-Pacific region" — single geography dependency for semiconductor manufacturing (TSMC primary, though not named in this section).

7. NO off-balance-sheet entities, SPVs, or VIEs disclosed in this MD&A section. Note 3 (operating leases), Note 12 (debt/purchase obligations), and Note 9 (non-affiliated investments) are referenced but not reproduced here — those notes would need separate extraction for investee enumeration and lease RVG analysis.

8. FY2025 capex guidance: $3.5B–$4.0B for property and equipment (no specific counterparty named in this section).

financial_statements_and_notes.notes:
[chunk 1/2] This is NVIDIA's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-02-21) financial statements and notes section. Key extraction findings:

1. COST_OPACITY (severity 2): In Feb 2023, NVIDIA extended depreciable lives of server/storage/network equipment from 3→4-5 years and assembly/test from 5→7 years, generating a $135M operating income benefit in FY2024. This is a material accounting policy change that inflates reported margins.

2. CAPEX_ROI_GAP (severity 3): $16.1B in outstanding inventory purchase and long-term supply/capacity obligations vs only $5.3B inventory on balance sheet. Excess/obsolete inventory provisions flagged as PwC critical audit matter — significant management judgment required on future demand assumptions.

3. HIDDEN_LEVERAGE (severity 2): $1.1B in data center operating leases not yet commenced (expected FY2025 start, 1-10 year terms), sitting off-balance-sheet as of Jan 28, 2024. This is incremental to the $1.35B present value of existing operating lease obligations already on-balance-sheet.

4. Non-marketable equity securities portfolio: The filing discloses accounting policy for private company investments (cost minus impairment + observable price changes), with $985M invested in non-affiliated entities in FY2024 cash flows. Note 8 (non-marketable equity securities detail) appears to be cut off in this excerpt — individual investee names not yet visible. A full Note 8 extraction would enumerate CoreWeave, Lambda, Figure AI, xAI, Mistral, Cohere, Perplexity, etc.

5. Arm/SoftBank deal termination: $1.4B write-off in FY2023 — historical but context for NVIDIA's strategic relationship with SoftBank.

6. Operating leases total: $1.539B undiscounted, $1.347B PV, weighted avg term 6.1 years at 3.76% discount rate. No residual value guarantees disclosed.
[chunk 2/2] Key findings from NVIDIA FY2024 10-K financial notes:

1. PURCHASE COMMITMENTS ($20.7B total): Heavily front-loaded — $17.3B due in FY2025 alone. Includes $16.1B inventory/supply obligations and $3.5B multi-year cloud service agreements. This creates significant execution risk if demand softens.

2. PREPAID SUPPLY ($4.96B combined): $2.458B long-term + $2.5B short-term prepaid supply and capacity agreements — NVIDIA is paying upfront to secure supply, creating capex ROI gap risk. No specific counterparties named (likely TSMC, SK Hynix, etc.).

3. NON-MARKETABLE EQUITY ($1.321B): Portfolio grew 4.6x YoY from $288M to $1.321B via $859M net additions in FY2024. One investment had a secondary raise generating $178M unrealized gain. No individual investees named in this section (cross-reference Note 9 / separate equity securities note for names like CoreWeave, etc.). The circularity risk is real: NVIDIA invests in compute customers who then buy NVIDIA GPUs.

4. CUSTOMER CONCENTRATION: One unnamed customer = 13% of FY2024 revenue (~$7.9B) in Compute & Networking. Two customers = 24% + 11% of AR. High concentration in a segment driven by AI infrastructure buildout.

5. CHINA REVENUE ($10.3B, ~17% of total): Material exposure subject to escalating US export controls — cross-reference Item 1A risk factors for H100/A100 restrictions.

6. EXCESS INVENTORY OBLIGATIONS: $1.655B on balance sheet; $1.4B expensed in FY2024 for obligations exceeding demand — signals supply chain over-commitment risk.

7. This section does NOT name individual private equity investees (CoreWeave, Lambda, etc.) — those appear in a separate non-marketable equity roster not included in this text excerpt. The $1.321B aggregate is extracted; individual investee nodes should be added when that roster section is processed.
